**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data), Section 13 / ¶p0088.**

- **Issue:** Garman is declared owner of all IP in the Work "including any Improvements **or Modifications**", with no title passing to Sparkling. The Modifications are the bespoke Schedule "D" changes Sparkling commissions and pays for under the Fee Schedule, so paid-for deliverables vest entirely in the vendor. The only rights back are the Section 2 licence (non-exclusive, non-transferable, tied to AS400s at Authorized Locations) plus Section 3 restrictions (no sublicence, no modification) — short of the fallback's perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense. There is also no statement that Sparkling retains rights in its own data, despite Garman converting that data under Section 4.
- **Not flagged:** Garman's ownership of its underlying Software platform and Improvements, and Garman's retention of the escrowed Source Code — consistent with the playbook.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** removes Modifications from Garman's ownership statement, assigns paid-for Modifications/deliverables to Sparkling, adds a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back to any embedded Garman IP (overriding Section 3), confirms Sparkling's data remains Sparkling's, and bars joint ownership — with the licence-only fallback offered in the comment.
